To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The sorghum aphids are not as destructive as the shoot fly and stem borer.
the aphid population build-up was high on the susceptible lines and cultivars and the resistant lines and cultivars had a low population of sorghum aphids.
sorghum aphids are a serious pest of sorghum and that there is a need for developing aphid-resistant sorghum varieties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a reliable screening technique for resistance to sorghan aphid, Melanapis sacchari, which is a major insect pest of sorghum in India.
the development of a new method of controlling sorghum aphids by using the aphid’s natural enemies, the parasitoid wasp, Diaeretiella rapae, as a biological control agent.
developing a better understanding of the sorghum aphids, their biology, population dynamics, and the impact of the aphid on sorghum production.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
61526, 61558 and CSV 216 were promising for aphid resistance with a plant damaging index of < 40% and a population of < 20 aphids per leaf.
61526, 61558, RSV 158, RSV 160, RSV 162, RSV 163, C-43 and CSV 216 were promising with < 2 aphids per leaf and < 2 leaf chlorosis score during both seasons.
the sorghum aphids were not a threat to the sorghum crop in India.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

61526, 61558, 61559 and 61560 were the best aphid resistant genotypes, while 61526, C-43 and 61559 were the best genotypes with shoot fly and aphid resistance, 61558 was the best with aphid and midge resistance, 61560 was best with midge and aphid resistance and 61526 was the best with shoot fly, midge and aphids resistance.
the aphid resistant lines and the shoot fly resistant lines had a low aphid population with a low plant damaging score.
the aphid population was found to be high in all the genotypes during Rabi 06 and Khar 2006 seasons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the aphid resistance of 61526 is stable in different environments.
the sorghum aphids can be effectively managed by using resistant cultivars and by adopting the cultural practices.
the aphid population build-up was low and there was no significant impact of aphids on the sorghum yield.
